'''Real numbers''' are numbers that are either [[rational number|rational]] or [[number#Categories|irrational]].

== Formal definition ==

The set of all real numbers $\mathbb{R}$ is a '''complete''' [[field (mathematical concept)#Ordered_field|ordered field]].

Here, completeness means that any non-empty subset of $\mathbb{R}$ bounded above has a '''least upper bound''' in $\mathbb{R}$.

i.e.,

$$
\forall S \in \mathbb{R},\, S \ne \emptyset,\, \exists b: \forall s \in S, s \le b,\,  \\
\exists \operatorname{sup}(S) \in \mathbb{R}.
$$

=== Via [[Dedekind cut]] ===

$$
\mathbb{R}=\{A\subset\mathbb{Q}:A\text{ is a Dedekind cut}\}.
$$

Where each [[Dedekind cut]] $A$ is declared to be a real number.

{{Hidden proof}}
Recall:

{{#content:Q2400}}

To prove that the set of all Dedekind cuts is indeed a complete ordered field, recall the definition of [[field (mathematical concept)#Formal_definition|field]] and [[field (mathematical concept)#Ordered_field|orderness]].

'''Qualification as field''':

$$
A>B \iff B \subset A \tag{order} \\
0_\mathbb{R}=\{q\in\mathbb{Q}:q<0_\mathbb{Q}\} \tag{additive identity} \\
1_\mathbb{R}=\{q\in\mathbb{Q}:q<1_\mathbb{Q}\} \tag{multiplicative identity} \\
A+B=\{a+b:a\in A,\ b\in B\} \tag{addition} \\
-A=\{q\in\mathbb{Q}:\exists s\notin A,\, q<-s\} \tag{additive inverse} \\
A\cdot B=
\begin{cases}
\{q\in\mathbb{Q}:\exists a\in A,\ b\in B,\ q<ab\}, & A>0_\mathbb{R},\ B>0_\mathbb{R},\\
0_\mathbb{R}, & A=0_\mathbb{R} \lor B=0_\mathbb{R},\\
-\big(A\cdot(-B)\big), & A>0_\mathbb{R},\ B<0_\mathbb{R},\\
-\big((-A)\cdot B\big), & A<0_\mathbb{R},\ B>0_\mathbb{R},\\
(-A)\cdot(-B), & A<0_\mathbb{R},\ B<0_\mathbb{R}.
\end{cases} \tag{multiplication} \\
A^{-1}=
\begin{cases}
\left\{q\in\mathbb{Q}:\exists s\notin A\text,\, q<\frac{1}{s}\right\}, & A>0_\mathbb{R}, \\
-(-A)^{-1}, & A<0_\mathbb{R}.
\end{cases} \tag{multiplicative inverse}
$$

'''Completeness''':

Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a set of Dedekind cuts, then its supremum is simply the union of those Dedekind cuts, i.e.,

$$
\operatorname{sup}(\mathcal{A})=\bigcup_{A\in\mathcal{A}}A.
$$

which is itself a Dedekind cut, equal to the largest Dedekind cut in $\mathcal{A}$.

{{End hidden}}

== Properties ==

=== $\forall r \in \mathbb{R}: \exists n \in \mathbb{N},\, n>r$ (Archimedean property) ===

{{Hidden proof}}

$\forall r \in \mathbb{R}$, let

$$
n=
\begin{cases}
0, & r<0, \\
\lfloor r \rfloor +1, & \text{elsewise}.
\end{cases}
$$

where $\lfloor \rfloor$ is the [[floor function]].

then

$$
n \in \mathbb{N}, n>r
$$

{{End hidden}}
